title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.15600v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over long Web interaction histories, making memory management critical for reliable and efficient decision making. Existing methods primarily optimize storage, retrieval, or compression, but the memories most semantically relevant to the current state are not necessarily those that most improve the agent's action. We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility. MemCredit estimates the state-, reference-context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories through controlled counterfactual interventions, and distills these intervention-derived credits into a lightweight utility estimator. translated_title: MemCredit：长时程网络智能体决策时记忆从相关性到效用性的转变
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地在长篇网络交互历史中运行，这使得记忆管理对于可靠且高效的决策至关重要。现有方法主要优化存储、检索或压缩，但与当前状态语义最相关的记忆并不一定是最大程度改善智能体动作的记忆。我们提出了 MemCredit，一个以决策为中心的记忆框架，它将记忆选择从语义相关性转向决策效用。MemCredit 通过受控的反事实干预来估计单条记忆在状态、参考上下文和策略条件下的边际贡献，并将这些由干预得出的信用值蒸馏到一个轻量级的效用估计器中。在推理阶段，语义相关性仅用于高召回率的候选生成，而预测的效用则在固定的 token 预算下裁决哪些记忆被保留，无需修改……
tldr: MemCredit 提出以决策为中心的记忆框架，通过反事实干预衡量每条记忆对智能体决策的真实边际贡献，并将其蒸馏为轻量级效用估计器，使推理时的记忆筛选从语义相关性转向决策效用，从而在固定 token 预算下保留真正有助于决策的记忆。
en_tdlr: MemCredit shifts memory selection in long-horizon web agents from semantic relevance to decision utility by estimating each memory's marginal contribution through counterfactual interventions and distilling these credits into a lightweight utility estimator that arbitrates memory retention at inference time under a fixed token budget.
